RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-019, a
Resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale approving Conditional
Use Permit (CUP) 25-0005 and Modification (MOD) 25-0011, and find that the project is
categorically exempt from environmental review.

BACKGROUND

The original project to establish the major wireless telecommunications facility was
approved by the Planning Commission through CUP 02-13 (Resolution No. PC-2002-
048) on October 3, 2002. The facility became operational on October 15, 2002, and
expired on October 15, 2012, requiring a new application to remain operational.

Subsequently, the Planning Commission approved CUP 13-025 (Resolution No. PC-
2014-005) on February 13, 2014, for the continued operation and facility modifications,
which established an expiration date of February 25, 2024.
 Staff Report to the Planning Commission
CUP 25-0005 and MOD 25-0011
September 11, 2025
Page 2

Since the original approval, the existing facility has undergone six modifications consisting
of the relocation, removal, or replacement of existing equipment, installation of new or
upgraded equipment, and construction of new equipment cabinets or enclosures through
various MOD applications:

    MOD 12-001 approved on January 4, 2012;
    MOD 13-074 approved on September 24, 2014;
    CUP 13-025 MOD No. 1 approved on August 9, 2018;
    MOD 18-049 approved on October 2, 2018;
    MOD 20-064 approved on December 17, 2020; and,
    MOD 21-065 approved on January 13, 2022.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received prior to the expiration of
the major wireless telecommunications facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP
is required for the continued operation of the facility.

The formal applications for CUP 25-0005 and MOD 25-0011 were submitted on February
18, 2025, and June 3, 2025. After resolution of completeness items, the applications were
deemed complete on July 21, 2025, and scheduled for the September 11, 2025, Planning
Commission hearing.

ANALYSIS

The proposed project is a request to allow the continued operation of an existing major
wireless telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years and equipment upgrades to
an existing wireless telecommunications facility located at 2272 East Palmdale
Boulevard. Equipment upgrades consist of installing a new 36-inch microwave dish
antenna with accompanying radio for T-Mobile on the existing 65-foot monopole. The
facility consists of a 65-foot-high monopole within an approximately 730 square-foot
equipment enclosure. The existing facility is located on the south side of the undeveloped
portion of the parcel, approximately 200 feet south of the existing shopping center’s
southerly parking area, and will be accessed by an existing paved road.

undeveloped portion of the parcel, approximately 200 feet south of the existing shopping

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the proposed project
qualifies for a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under Section 15301, which exempts
operation, permitting, or minor alteration of existing, public or private structures, facilities,
or mechanical equipment involving negligible or no expansion of existing or former use.
This exemption applies to the new microwave dish antenna to be installed on the existing
monopole within the existing equipment enclosure. The project will not result in significant
environmental impacts and does not require mitigation measures, as it will be carried out
within an existing equipment enclosure and on an existing wireless communications
facility that does not contain environmentally sensitive areas. Thus, no further
environmental documentation or analysis is required.

  RESOLUTION NO. PC-2025-019

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  PALMDALE APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 25-0005 AND
  MODIFICATION 25-0011; A REQUEST TO ALLOW THE CONTINUED
  OPERATION OF A MAJOR WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS
  FACILITY AND EQUIPMENT UPGRADES TO AN EXISTING FACILITY
  LOCATED AT 2272 EAST PALMDALE BOULEVARD, AND FIND THE
  PROJECT IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM ENVIRONMENTAL
  REVIEW

  WHEREAS, Justin Robinson, on behalf of 2200 Town Square East, LLC, has filed
an application requesting the approval of Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 25-0005 and
Modification (MOD) 25-0011, to allow the continued operation of a major wireless
telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years and equipment upgrades to an
existing wireless telecommunications facility, as described herein (hereinafter referred
to as “Application”); and,

  WHEREAS, The Application applies to a wireless telecommunications facility
located at 2272 East Palmdale Boulevard, identified on the Los Angeles County
Assessor roll as Assessor Parcel Number 3018-028-031, legally described in Exhibit A
hereto and shown on the map attached hereto as Exhibit B; and,

  WHEREAS, the original facility was approved by the Planning Commission
through CUP 02-13 (Resolution No. PC-2002-048) on October 3, 2002, became
operational on October 15, 2002, and expired on October 15, 2012; and,

  WHEREAS, continued operation and modification of the facility was subsequently
approved by the Planning Commission through CUP 13-025 (Resolution No. PC-2014-
005) on February 13, 2014, with an expiration date of February 25, 2024; and,

  WHEREAS, On September 11, 2025, the Planning Commission of the City of
Palmdale conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the Application and concluded said
hearing on that date.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE, AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all of the
facts set forth in the foregoing Recitals are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to
the environmental document:
 Resolution No. PC-2025-019
CUP 25-0005 and MOD 25-0011
Page 2

  A  Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the proposed
  project qualifies for a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under Section 15301,
  which exempts operation, permitting, or minor alteration of existing, public
  or private structures, facilities, or mechanical equipment involving negligible
  or no expansion of existing or former use. This exemption applies to the
  new microwave dish antenna to be installed on the existing monopole within
  the existing equipment enclosure. The project will not result in significant
  environmental impacts and does not require mitigation measures, as it will
  be carried out within an existing equipment enclosure and on an existing
  wireless communications facility that does not contain environmentally
  sensitive areas. Thus, no further environmental documentation or analysis
  is required.

  B  The custodian of records for the environmental document and all other
  materials which constitute the record of proceedings upon which the
  Planning Commission’s decision is based is the Planning Manager of the
  City of Palmdale. These documents are available for public review in the
  Planning Division of the City of Palmdale located at 38250 Sierra Highway,
  Palmdale, California 93550, telephone 661/267-5200.

  SECTION 3. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission
during the above-referenced September 11, 2025, public hearing, including public
testimony, and written and oral staff report, this Commission specifically finds as follows:

  A  The proposed use is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives of
  the General Plan; (CUP)

  B  The request is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives of the
  General Plan; (MOD)

  The major wireless telecommunications facility is located within the
  Educational Flex (EDFX) General Plan Land Use designation and zone,
  and is consistent with the policies and objectives of the General Plan as
  shown in Exhibit C. More specifically, the project is consistent with General
  Plan Goal PFSI-4.2, as the existing wireless telecommunications facility will
  continue providing necessary telecommunication services to the area
  without the need to build additional structures nearby. In addition, the
  proposed modification to install a new 36-inch microwave dish antenna with
  accompanying radio for T-Mobile on the existing 65-foot monopole,
  enhances broadband connectivity and capacity to the existing eligible
  wireless facility by using the least intrusive means to expand coverage in
  this underserved area.
 Resolution No. PC-2025-019
CUP 25-0005 and MOD 25-0011
Page 3

  C  The proposed use is beneficial and desirous to the community and is
  consistent with the purpose, intent and standards of this Title and other
  applicable ordinances and codes adopted by the City; (CUP)

  D  The proposed structure or addition meets all applicable ordinance
  standards including, but not limited to, minimum structure design,
  development standards and setbacks. (MOD)

  The proposed project is beneficial and desirable to the community as it
  supports the continued operation and upgrade of a major wireless
  telecommunications facility, enhancing local connectivity while minimizing
  visual and environmental impacts. By maintaining and improving an
  existing facility rather than constructing a new one, the project avoids
  greater disruption to the surrounding area and aligns with the intent and
  purpose of the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC). The project meets all
  applicable ordinance standards, including minimum structure design,
  development standards, and setbacks as demonstrated in Exhibit D. No
  increase in height or square footage is proposed. The existing antennas
  will remain flush-mounted, and the color scheme continues to blend with
  the surroundings, minimizing visual impact. All ground-mounted equipment
  will remain screened within the existing enclosure, ensuring full compliance
  with current PMC requirements. Although the facility is located on the
  eastern property line with a non-conforming side yard setback, all other
  setback requirements are met, including the 10-foot front and rear
  setbacks. Since its original approval, the City has undergone a General
  Plan Update (Palmdale 2045) and Zoning Ordinance update (Ordinance
  No. 1603), which modified the zone from General Commercial (C-3) to
  EDFX, modifying the development standards. The proposed location is
  acceptable since removal and replacement of the existing facility would be
  more invasive to the surrounding area.

  E  The proposed use and the ongoing operation of the use will not have a
  substantial adverse effect on abutting property or the allowed use thereof,
  and will not generate excessive noise, vibration, traffic, or other
  disturbances, nuisances, or hazards; (CUP)

  F  The site for the proposed use has adequate pedestrian and vehicular
  access; (CUP)

  G  The request complies with the purpose and intent of all applicable terms
  and conditions of the existing entitlement; (MOD)

  The proposed use and ongoing operation of the facility will not have a
  substantial adverse effect on the environment or abutting properties. The
 Resolution No. PC-2025-019
CUP 25-0005 and MOD 25-0011
Page 4

  existing facility is located on the south side of the undeveloped portion of
  the parcel, approximately 200 feet south of the existing shopping center’s
  southerly parking area, and is surrounded by an existing school and a
  vacant lot zoned for educational facilities. Per the plans date stamped
  “Received June 6, 2025,” the project will maintain its original design
  featuring antennas flush-mounted to the pole, colors that blend with the
  surrounding environment, and an enclosure to continue abating noise
  produced by the equipment. The existing facility will be accessed via an
  existing paved road, with only periodic trips to the site required for routine
  maintenance after the upgrades are completed. The intermittent parking
  needs of this use will be accommodated through the existing parking lot
  improvements on the site, ensuring there will be no impact on any other
  access points or parking requirements in the vicinity. The proposed use is
  consistent with the policies and objectives of the General Plan, as shown
  in Exhibit C, and is permitted under PMC Section 17.47.020 subject to the
  approval of a CUP.

  H  The request is listed in Subsection (B) of PMC Section 17.26.040 (Minor
  modifications to approved plans) and does not require new land use
  entitlements, including but not limited to a conditional use permit or site
  plan review; (MOD)

  The proposed modification to install a new 36-inch microwave dish antenna
  with accompanying radio for T-Mobile on the existing 65-foot monopole
  does not significantly alter the site plan as approved by CUP 13-025. The
  modifications are permitted under PMC Section 17.26.040(B)(1)(i), which
  allows minor modifications to previously approved existing facilities
  pursuant to PMC Section 17.95.010 (Communication/wireless
  telecommunication facilities).

  I  There has not been more than one other minor modification application for
  the same project within the past 12 months; and (MOD)

  MOD 25-0011 has been the only minor modification application for this
